parts.label: b

parts.reason: S2.3 covers measures of variation including quartiles/percentiles from grouped/stem-leaf data with linear interpolation.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Mean and standard deviation from summary statistics
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers calculating standard deviation including from summary statistics (Sxx) and mean.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Pearson's skewness coefficient (mean-mode)/sd
parts.reason: No statement mentions this named skewness measure or formula; S2.3/S2.4 cover central tendency, variation and outlier interpretation but not a skewness coefficient. A named concept absent from the statements makes the part OUT.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Comparing distributions using summary statistics
parts.reason: S2.3/S2.4 cover drawing inferences and interpretations from measures of central tendency and variation between two distributions.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Show Syy formula and calculate PMCC
parts.reason: Syy from summary statistics is S2.3 (Sxx formula), in spec. Calculating r: S5.1 states calculation of correlation coefficients is excluded and formula use is not required, BUT S5.1 also explicitly states students will be expected to calculate r using their calculator, which is an in-spec alternative method that earns full marks even though the mark scheme shows the formula.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Interpret PMCC value
parts.reason: S2.2 covers understanding informal interpretation of correlation; since obtaining r itself is achievable via the in-spec calculator method (S5.1), interpreting that value is in spec and does not depend on an excluded step.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Consistency of PMCC with linear model belief
parts.reason: S2.2 covers interpretation of correlation and appropriateness of a linear model; this follows from the in-spec (calculator-based) r value, not an excluded calculation.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Regression line equation w = a + by
parts.reason: EXPLICIT EXCLUSION S2.2: 'calculations involving regression lines are excluded'. This part requires calculating the regression coefficients, which is directly excluded.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Use regression equation to predict weight
parts.reason: This part only makes sense using the regression equation found in the excluded part (d); per the dependency rule this is OUT.

parts.label: c

parts.reason: S4.2 covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Justification for histogram use (continuous data)
parts.reason: S2.1 covers histograms and their use for representing (continuous) data.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Estimating frequency from histogram using area = frequency
parts.reason: S2.1 explicitly states area in a histogram represents frequency, and this technique is required for the estimate.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Median estimate via linear interpolation on grouped/histogram data
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly requires linear interpolation to calculate percentiles (including median) from grouped data.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Assessing suitability of Normal model using mean vs median
parts.reason: S4.3 covers selecting/critiquing appropriateness of the Normal model; S2.3 supports use of mean/median comparison as evidence.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding constant from cumulative distribution function
parts.reason: S4.1 covers discrete probability distributions; using F(6)=1 to find k is a basic property of a distribution, not an excluded mean/variance calculation.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Deriving probability distribution from cdf
parts.reason: S4.1 covers discrete probability distributions; constructing the pmf from differences of the cdf is distribution construction, not the excluded mean/variance calculation.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Forming simultaneous equations using sum of probabilities and E(Y)
parts.reason: EXPLICIT EXCLUSION S4.1: calculation of mean of a discrete random variable is excluded. Forming the second equation requires applying the E(Y)=Σy·P(Y=y) formula, which is the excluded mean calculation, even though the target value E(Y)=4.02 is given.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Calculating E(Y^2)
parts.reason: EXPLICIT EXCLUSION S4.1: calculation of mean/variance of discrete random variables is excluded; E(Y^2) is used to compute variance and is excluded, and also depends on the value of b found in the excluded part (c).

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Variance of linear transformation of discrete random variable
parts.reason: EXPLICIT EXCLUSION S4.1: variance of discrete random variables is excluded; this part also depends on results from the excluded parts (c) and (d).

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Probability of sum of two independent discrete random variables
parts.reason: S3.1 covers independent events probability calculations. The only probability value needed from the excluded chain, a=0.15, is given directly in the question ('show that a=0.15'), and P(X=1) etc. come from the in-spec part (b), so this part does not depend on any excluded working.

parts.reason: S3.2 covers calculating combined probabilities via tree diagrams.

parts.label: c

parts.reason: S3.2 combined with basic algebra (P2.6) to solve for n; this is standard use of probability formulae plus algebraic solving, both in spec.

parts.label: d

parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly covers conditional probability calculations including P(A|B) formula application via tree diagrams.

parts.reason: S4.2 covers use of the Normal distribution, including questions that may involve solving simultaneous equations for parameters.

parts.reason: S2.4 explicitly covers identifying outliers using a specified rule (e.g. Q1-1.5×IQR/Q3+1.5×IQR), and S4.2 covers finding Normal probabilities; combining these is in spec.
